title: BAGMAN AuditEvent
description: Canonical, append-oriented `AuditEvent` (PID §13-15). Records something meaningful that happened inside BAGMAN. Audit events are immutable after creation, UTC timestamped, actor-attributed, correlation-aware, and causally traceable. This schema is CD-2's foundation event contract; CD-2 need only implement the foundation event taxonomy (see `event_type` below) — later deliveries will add further event types without breaking this contract.

audit_event_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this audit event.

event_type.description: The kind of event that occurred. Deliberately open (NOT a closed enum) so future event types can be added without schema redesign. CD-2's own foundation event set (documentation only, not an enforced closed set): `ENTITY_REGISTERED`, `SOURCE_REGISTERED`, `EVIDENCE_OBSERVED`, `EVIDENCE_REGISTERED`, `EXTERNAL_REFERENCE_LINKED`, `PROVENANCE_RECORDED`. Later deliveries are expected to add further event types (e.g. `CLASSIFICATION_PROPOSED`, `RECONCILIATION_CONFIRMED`, and others from PID §13's longer illustrative list) — those are NOT implemented in CD-2 and are named here only to document the taxonomy's future direction.

occurred_at.description: UTC timestamp at which the recorded event occurred.

actor_type.description: The category of actor that caused this event. PID §14 gives this exact closed list and does not ask for extensibility here (unlike `entity_type` / `source_type` / `evidence_type` / evidence `status` elsewhere in these contracts), so this is a closed JSON Schema `enum`.

actor_id.description: Identifies the SPECIFIC actor that caused this event, e.g. `"matt"`, `"bagman-agent"`, `"mail-ingest-worker"`, `"reconciler"`, `"chargebee"`. Must not be a generic literal such as `"system"` alone — PID §14 explicitly instructs BAGMAN not to represent all activity as system, since that destroys accountability.

subject_type.description: The canonical BAGMAN object type this event is about, e.g. `EvidenceItem`, `GovernedEntity`, `Source`.

subject_id.description: Canonical identifier of the subject object (of type `subject_type`) this event is about.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared by every audit event belonging to the same multi-step workflow/operational story (PID §15). Every audit event must belong to a correlation.

causation_id.description: The `audit_event_id` of the event that directly caused this one, forming a causal chain within a `correlation_id`. This field is REQUIRED (the key must always be present) and is `null` ONLY for the first event in a causal chain — a caller cannot omit causation silently; it must be stated explicitly, even when there is none yet.

payload.description: Structured, event-specific detail. Must NEVER contain secrets, credentials, or full evidence-content bodies (PID §36) — audit events must be safe to log. Keep payloads to canonical object references and small structured facts, not raw document/email contents.

schema_version.description: Contract version identifier for this AuditEvent record. Must literally equal `"bagman.audit_event.v1"` for instances of this schema version.
